segments.d6d727d651: Shilika Jain is a senior fractional PR operator for Web3, AI and cybersecurity founders. Six years. 50+ protocols. Forbes, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block, Blockworks and AI Magazine placements. APAC reach across Korea, Japan, Vietnam, Singapore, India and the UAE. Currently leads PR & partnerships at Myosin, a growth-marketing DAO. Previously built CoinMarketCap's APAC PR function. Direct line to 200+ vetted Web3 KOLs.
segments.9ed08cd041: If a Web3, AI or cybersecurity founder needs to be in <1>Forbes, CoinDesk, Cointelegraph, Decrypt, The Block, Blockworks or AI Magazine</1> in the next 90 days, Shilika is the operator who runs that play. Not a junior account handler. Not a content factory. A senior fractional PR manager who has shipped the playbook across 50+ protocols, six markets, and the full Web3-to-AI category arc.
segments.0259ed81ff: The model is <1>fractional</1> on purpose. Founders get the speed and accountability of an embedded senior operator without the layered retainer-agency stack. Engagements are bounded, named, and tied to outlet-level outcomes. The opposite of a deck-driven monthly retainer.
segments.c5fbadec1a: Five workstreams that combine across most engagements:
segments.09e0a0c833: <1>Strategic PR campaigns</1>Tier-1 outreach, embargo strategy, launch sprints, crisis communications and sentiment reporting.
segments.6d565822cd: <1>Founder profiling & op-eds</1>Op-ed ghostwriting, podcast tours, speaker placement, LinkedIn and X positioning for technical founders.
segments.f72bf39a27: <1>KOL & influencer marketing</1>Campaign design, creator vetting, performance tracking and token-launch operations across 200+ vetted Web3 KOLs.
segments.fccc1d8239: <1>APAC localisation & access</1>Native translation, regional KOL networks and on-ground journalist relationships across Korea, Japan, Vietnam, China and India.
segments.cd2d00883a: <1>GTM and TGE communications</1>Pre-launch sequencing, exchange relations (Binance, OKX, MEXC), community seeding and post-launch sentiment management.
segments.16e3c0a715: Most engagements blend three or four of these. A pure "press release service" almost never wins. The work that lands is a category narrative, a named founder voice, an outlet that fits the story, and a calendar moment that anchors the news cycle.

segments.d3935ce6d4: Three engagement shapes cover most of the inbound:
segments.52c0b6440d: <1>Fractional retainer</1> — $3,000 to $7,000 per month for ongoing senior-operator capacity. Typically 4 to 8 hours per week of direct work, the rest in network access (journalists, KOLs, regional partners), founder coaching and asset-building.
segments.3df057ce7b: <1>Launch sprint</1> — $15,000 to $40,000 for a single dated event: a TGE, a mainnet, a funding announcement, a category-defining op-ed series. 6 to 10 weeks. Outcome is named-outlet placement, not impressions.
segments.84c0841b3d: <1>Productized content</1> — Founder Essay Package ($3,500), Whitepaper Sprint ($9,500), Op-Ed of the Month ($2,500/mo, 3-month minimum). For founders who need the writing work without the full PR retainer. <2>Content writing service page.</2>
segments.29f76c8261: The first call is a free 30-minute teardown: what story you are sitting on, which outlets it actually fits, and which playbook is the right one. No deck. No discovery sprint. The intent is to see if the work is real.
segments.e62ced1194: "The whole point of fractional senior-operator PR is that you find out in 30 minutes whether the campaign is real. If it isn't, that's a feature." — Shilika Jain

segments.537fb7a83e: How is fractional PR different from a PR agency?
segments.c16050c8ef: Fractional PR is a senior operator embedded in the team without the layered junior-account-handler stack. Faster decisions, fewer briefings, direct founder access. Less hand-holding on day-one onboarding, less brand-level production. The trade-offs are mapped out in the <1>fractional-vs-agency comparison</1>.
